facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: Three features limit how far this base can be used. First, it is a pre-acquisition picture. The signed Megger purchase (approximately $2.35 billion, of which $0.9 billion is cash) is to be financed by a new $1.5 billion committed facility set that will replace the existing facility at closing, so the debt table at June 30, 2026 describes a structure management expects to retire. Second, the LTM period carries the Maritime acquisition (closed April 25, 2025) for all four quarters, but FY2025 and 9M 2025 carry it only from that date, so year-on-year growth includes acquired revenue, and the latest nine months include a large working capital inflow and a large discontinued-operations outflow, so LTM cash conversion is not a clean run rate. Third, the 10-Q Q3 prints nine-month cash flows only, so discrete Q3 cash flow is not available.

facts.label: Leverage

This is a bound on method, not a forecast, and Megger EBITDA is Not supplied.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: ESCO is a publicly listed group with no sponsor or parent named in the context or the filings; material US subsidiaries guarantee the bank facility (10-K page:80). It reports three segments: Aerospace & Defense (A&D), Utility Solutions Group (USG) and RF Test & Measurement (Test). A&D has grown from 34% of continuing revenue in 2023 to 44% in 2025, reflecting Navy growth and the Maritime acquisition, which makes the group more dependent on US and UK naval programs and on government funding. The group sold its Space business (VACCO) in July 2025 and used the proceeds mainly to repay debt, so fiscal 2025 and the first nine months of fiscal 2026 show deleveraging rather than distributions.

Closing was expected in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, which began October 1, 2026, so by the 2026-11-05 as-of date the transaction may have closed. No supplied source is dated after August 10, 2026, so closing status, the debt actually drawn and the size of TBG AG's resulting stake are Not supplied.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Financing and new debt. The cash portion "will be funded through existing cash on hand and incremental debt, with committed financing in place" (10-Q Q3 page:19). On May 29, 2026 ESCO and certain subsidiaries entered into a Credit Agreement, the New Credit Facility, with JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as administrative agent. It provides a senior secured revolving credit facility of $500 million, a senior secured term loan A of $500 million and a senior secured term loan B of $500 million. It becomes effective only on, and substantially concurrently with, closing and replaces the Existing Credit Facility. The revolver and term loan A mature five years after the effective date and term loan B seven years after (10-Q Q3 page:12). Foreign subsidiaries may also draw. tables.title: Issuer sources relied on — Source (exact name)

rows.label: ESCO is a listed, sponsor-free aerospace, utility-testing and RF-testing group with a large backlog. Its pending Megger acquisition, with equity valued at about $1.4 billion and cash of $0.9 billion, is the main change for creditors.
Three segments serve aerospace and defense, electric utilities and RF testing; the US Government accounted for approximately 23% of fiscal 2025 revenue and no customer exceeded 10%.
Backlog was $1,540.5 million at June 30, 2026, with approximately 59% expected to convert to revenue in the next twelve months.
Megger, a named competitor of the utility segment, is to be bought from TBG AG for approximately $2.35 billion, and TBG AG will sign a shareholder agreement.
Documented capital allocation since fiscal 2025 shows debt paydown after the VACCO sale and a small dividend, with no share repurchases and no creditor-adverse actions in the sources.
The existing $500 million revolving facility and term loan A are to be replaced by new $500 million revolver and two $500 million term loans at closing.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: ESCO has very low reported leverage and strong cover. Total borrowings were USD 85.0 million at June 30, 2026, down from USD 186.0 million at September 30, 2025, so total debt to EBITDA fell from 0.758x to 0.278x and net debt to EBITDA from 0.345x to 0.038x. EBITDA covered cash interest paid 20.42x on an LTM basis against 14.09x for FY2025 [CP-1 Chart data]. The mechanism was operating cash flow from continuing operations of USD 193.377 million in nine months 2026 funding net repayment and other uses, so the debt reduction came from cash generation, which supports debt service capacity [CP-1 Narrative review: leverage].

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: ESCO has ample liquidity and a short near-term maturity profile. Cash was USD 73.236 million and the revolver had USD 442.300 million undrawn after USD 12.7 million of letters of credit, together USD 515.536 million; USD 20.000 million of term loan A is current and USD 65.000 million falls due by August 30, 2028, which is the maturity of the existing revolver and term loan A [CP-1 Chart data]. The existing facility is secured by guarantees from material US subsidiaries and a pledge of equity of material foreign subsidiaries [CP-1 Debt instruments and facilities]. Because the facility is to be replaced at the Megger closing, this maturity profile is a pre-closing picture. The wording of the current portion changed from voluntary in Q1 2026 to obligated in Q2 and Q3 2026, a logged conflict the supplied documents do not explain [CP-1A Conflicts].

Continuing operating cash flow of USD 193.377 million benefited from customer advances, with contract liabilities up USD 71.5 million, and discontinued operations used USD 59.340 million, alongside approximately USD 59 million of cash tax paid on the VACCO gain. LTM free cash flow of USD 258.102 million is therefore a continuing-operations figure before that one-time outflow and before dividends [CP-1 Narrative review: cash flow quality]. Customer advances can reverse as projects deliver, which would lower operating cash flow.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: ESCO's acquisition will change the credit. The Megger purchase has total consideration of approximately USD 2.35 billion, of which USD 0.9 billion is cash and approximately USD 1.4 billion is ESCO equity, with closing expected in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 [CP-1A Transaction summary]. Committed financing is a new senior secured revolver, term loan A and term loan B of USD 500 million each, effective only at closing and replacing the existing facility [CP-1 Debt instruments and facilities]. Megger's financials are not supplied, so post-closing leverage and cover are not calculable. As a bound only, CP-1 shows that if the full USD 0.9 billion cash consideration were borrowed on top of current debt, total debt would be about 3.22x ESCO-only LTM EBITDA before Megger earnings; this is an Analyst Inference, not a forecast [CP-1 Narrative review: leverage]. The 2026-11-05 as-of date falls after the start of the expected closing quarter, and nothing after August 10, 2026 is supplied, so closing status is unknown.

Headroom is therefore not calculable, and the reported ratios in this credit view are not covenant ratios.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: ESCO's observed conduct supports creditors, and ownership will change. VACCO proceeds were used mainly to pay down debt, dividends are small, there were no buybacks in fiscal 2025 or Q3 2026 and no creditor-adverse action appears in the supplied sources. TBG AG will receive ESCO shares and sign a shareholder agreement at completion; its stake, governance rights and lock-up terms are not supplied [CP-1A Ownership, governance and sponsor behaviour].

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: ESCO's strengths start with its balance sheet. Reported leverage is low (total debt to EBITDA 0.278x) and cash interest cover is high (20.42x) on LTM figures, giving the issuer capacity to absorb a cost or volume shock before the acquisition financing [CP-1 Chart data; Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation]. Liquidity of USD 515.536 million is dominated by an undrawn revolver that matures August 30, 2028, so near-term refinancing risk is low [CP-1 Chart data; Documentary Fact]. Backlog of USD 1,540.5 million and a three-segment mix with no customer above 10% of sales support revenue visibility and limit single-customer risk [CP-1A Company and operating model; Documentary Fact]. Capital allocation since fiscal 2025 has favoured creditors, with debt repaid from divestiture proceeds, small dividends and no buybacks [CP-1A Ownership, governance and sponsor behaviour; Documentary Fact]. Cash generation from continuing operations was strong in the latest period [CP-1 Narrative review; Documentary Fact, qualified by working capital timing].

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: ESCO's weaknesses concentrate on the pending transaction and on missing documents. The Megger purchase is large relative to the existing debt, is funded partly with new term debt, and its terms and Megger's earnings are not supplied, so the leverage that creditors will face is unknown [CP-1A Transaction summary; Insufficient Information, with the missing datapoints being the credit agreement, Megger financials and closing status]. Covenant levels and headroom are missing for both the existing and the new facility [CP-1 Covenants and definitions; Insufficient Information]. Government funding concentration in Aerospace & Defense, termination for convenience and fixed-price cost risk could affect the largest and fastest-growing segment [CP-1A Credit translations; Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation]. Operating cash flow was lifted by customer advances and the reported free cash flow excludes a discontinued-operations outflow, so cash conversion is flattered in the nine months [CP-1 Narrative review: cash flow quality; Analyst Interpretation]. TBG AG's resulting stake and governance rights are unknown, which limits the view of control and alignment after closing [CP-1A Ownership, governance and sponsor behaviour; Insufficient Information]. Smaller weaknesses are renewables exposure in the utility segment, sole-source suppliers, and internal-control scope that excludes recently acquired businesses until they are tested [CP-1A Company and operating model; Documentary Fact].

spans.text: # CP-0 source readiness: ESCO TECHNOLOGIES INC (ese)
## Request
- Issuer: ESCO TECHNOLOGIES INC (issuer id `ese`, NYSE: ESE), registrant of all three filing types supplied, as of 2026-11-05, information cutoff 2026-11-05 (context).
- Run `ese-2026-11-05-credit_snapshot-host`, pathway `credit_snapshot`. Requested consumers: CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5 (the launcher's minimum set). CP-0 runs first and has no upstream handoff.
- Execution: host session. The host read the pinned source text and wrote this answer. No provider was called.

- Periods and currency (context): current period `q3-2026`, prior period `fy-2025`, reporting currency USD. ESCO has a September fiscal year end, so "Q3 2026" is the fiscal quarter ended June 30, 2026 and "FY2025" is the year ended September 30, 2025. The 10-Q says so: 10-Q Q3 page:4 "References to the third quarters of 2026 and 2025 represent the fiscal quarters ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively." The statements are in thousands of USD (10-Q Q3 page:2 "(Dollars in thousands, except per share amounts)"); the narrative text uses millions. No other currency is the reporting currency.
- Question: can the supplied public filings support CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5, and what remains blocked?
- Assertion: SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY; CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED. No credit conclusion, legal interpretation or investment opinion. No figure is normalized, reconciled or calculated here.
## Sources

### Labels used below

"10-K" is the FY2025 10-K. "10-Q Q1", "10-Q Q2" and "10-Q Q3" are the three 10-Qs. "Release Q1", "Release Q2" and "Release Q3" are the three EX-99.1 releases. The retrieval record (`_retrieval.json`) is pack metadata, not a source, and was ignored by the launcher.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The seven supplied filings can support a credit snapshot of ESCO as of the quarter ended June 30, 2026, with limitations. The pending Megger acquisition and its new financing are described only in summary form. | Medium | Megger's own financials, the 2026 credit agreement and the covenant levels are not supplied, so a post-acquisition leverage view cannot be sourced. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Audited FY2025 statements and unaudited statements for the three later quarters are located, with the VACCO business shown as discontinued operations. | Gives a reported financial base; comparisons must stay on continuing operations. | High |

| The existing $500 million revolver and incremental term loan mature August 30, 2028 and are to be replaced when the Megger deal closes. | Current debt terms are temporary; the new structure rests on an agreement that is not supplied. | Medium |
| Covenants are named as a leverage ratio and an interest coverage ratio, but required levels and reported ratios are not printed. | Covenant headroom cannot be sourced from these filings. | High |

| Nothing dated after August 10, 2026 is supplied, and management expected Megger to close in the first quarter of fiscal 2027. | Closing status at the as-of date is unknown, so debt may already have changed. | Medium |
| Earnings releases carry management-defined adjusted measures that the filings do not show. | Use filings for amounts and treat adjusted figures as attributed management claims. | Medium |
### Readiness view

The effective source set is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for all four requested consumers. The sources are filed statements, filed notes and management releases for one registrant, all dated before the 2026-11-05 cutoff, and they cover the audited FY2025 year and each fiscal quarter since. They do not contain the documents that would govern the pending change in the capital structure: the Megger share purchase agreement, the May 29, 2026 credit agreement, any Megger financial statements, or the existing credit agreement with its covenant definitions. Those gaps bound CP-2 and CP-1A rather than prevent them, because the 10-Q Q3 summarises the transaction and the new facility sizes. No consumer is CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED, and no downstream analytical handoff is treated as a source condition.
| Consumer | Status | Basis |

| CP-1 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Audited FY2025 statements and unaudited interim statements for all three later quarters are located with prior-year comparatives. Release adjusted measures and the interim contract-liability note need care (see Gaps). |
| CP-1A | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Business, segments, the VACCO sale, the Maritime acquisition and the Megger summary are located. Megger agreements and Megger financials are not supplied. |

| CP-2 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Facility-level debt, availability, letters of credit and the new facility sizes are located. Covenant levels, the new credit agreement terms and Megger's financials are not supplied, so headroom and pro forma leverage are not sourceable. |

### Source register

- Family and authority: filed annual report, original authority for audited FY2025, FY2024 and FY2023 consolidated statements. page:1 "For the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025"; signed December 1, 2025 (page:51 "December 1, 2025"). Commission file number 1-10596.

- Audit: page:51 index lists "Grant Thornton LLP, PCAOB ID Number 248"; page:55 "We have served as the Company’s auditor since 2021." The internal control opinion excludes the acquired Maritime business: page:56 "Our audit of, and opinion on, the Company’s internal control over financial reporting does not include the internal control over financial reporting of ESCO Maritime Solutions Ltd."

- Statements located: operations page:57, balance sheet pages:57 to 58, equity page:58, cash flows page:59. Debt note 7 on pages:80 to 81, which prints the revolving line of credit commitment: page:80 "The Credit Facility includes a $500 million revolving line of credit as well as provisions allowing for the increase of the credit facility commitment amount by an additional $250 million". Commitments note 11 on page:86. Leases note 12 starting page:86. Income tax note around page:79. MD&A liquidity on page:39.

- Perimeter: consolidated ESCO Technologies Inc. and subsidiaries, continuing operations. The VACCO business is recast: page:8 "VACCO is reflected as discontinued operations in the Consolidated Financial Statements and related notes for all periods shown in this Annual Report." The 10-K controls the recast FY2025 and FY2024 comparatives.

- Debt terms: page:80 "The financial covenants of the Credit Facility include a leverage ratio and an interest coverage ratio." and "The Credit Facility is secured by the unlimited guaranty of our direct and indirect material U.S. subsidiaries and the pledge of 100% of the equity interests of our direct and indirect material foreign subsidiaries." Levels are not printed.
- Units: thousands of USD in statements (page:57 "(Dollars in thousands, except per share amounts)").

- Pension: a search of all 89 10-K pages for pension, retiree, postretirement, defined benefit, retirement and savings plan found only the deferred tax asset line "Pension and other postretirement benefits" (page:79). No pension or retiree medical note is in the extracted text; see Gaps.
- Family and authority: filed unaudited quarterly report for the quarter ended December 31, 2025, filed 2026-02-09 per the pack retrieval record.

- Debt and liquidity pages:9 and 19: availability and cash are given as of December 31, 2025, and this 10-Q states the availability figure "excluding the Incremental Facility", a different basis from the 10-Q Q3. Short-term borrowings at foreign locations are also reported (page:19 "short-term borrowings at its foreign locations").
- Role: sequential quarter evidence. It is a separate active source; it does not replace the 10-K or later 10-Qs.
- Family and authority: filed unaudited quarterly report for the quarter ended March 31, 2026.
- Debt and liquidity page:11: availability and letters of credit at March 31, 2026, weighted average rates, and the statement "As of March 31, 2026, the Company was in compliance with all covenants."
- Megger: pages:18 and 24 give the April 15, 2026 agreement. Page:24 labels it a "Subsequent Event" at the March 31, 2026 balance sheet date.

- Family and authority: filed unaudited quarterly report for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, the latest filing supplied. Page:1 "QUARTERLY REPORT PURSUANT TO SECTION 13 OR 15(D) OF THE SECURITIES EXCHANGE ACT OF 1934 FOR THE QUARTERLY PERIOD ENDED JUNE 30, 2026". Signed page:31 "Dated: August 10, 2026".

- Statements located: three-month operations page:2, nine-month operations page:2, comprehensive income page:2, balance sheet pages:2 to 3, nine-month cash flows pages:3 to 4. The balance sheet compares June 30, 2026 with September 30, 2025. Cash flow has nine-month periods only; no discrete three-month cash flow is printed in this filing.

- Notes: segments pages:6 to 10 (A&D, USG, Test, with segment profit, D&A, assets and capex by quarter and nine months, for both years), debt note 7 pages:10 to 12, revenue disaggregation pages:13 to 15, remaining performance obligations page:16, leases note 12 pages:16 to 18, acquisition note 15 page:19.

- Debt and liquidity: page:10 "The Existing Credit Facility matures August 30, 2028, with balance due by this date." Page:11 "The letters of credit issued and outstanding under the Credit Facility totaled $12.7 million at June 30, 2026." and "As of June 30, 2026, the Company was in compliance with all covenants." The debt table (page:10) shows the revolver and the incremental term loan A separately, with the current portion.

- New facility: page:12 "The New Credit Facility will become effective subject to several conditions" and "will replace the Existing Credit Facility on the Transaction closing date". Sizes and tenors are on that page; the agreement itself is an exhibit incorporated by reference (page:30 "Exhibit 10.1 to the Company’s Form 8-K filed June 3, 2026") and is not supplied.

- Transaction: page:19 "The Company expects to complete the acquisition in the first quarter of fiscal 2027." The 8-Ks of April 15, 2026 and April 16, 2026 are referred to for terms (page:19) and are not supplied.

- Financing cost in the period: page:23 "approximately $7 million of debt financing costs incurred in the third quarter of 2026 related to the pending Megger acquisition" sits inside interest expense, net.
#### Earnings releases (EX-99.1)

- Family and authority: management-prepared, unaudited press releases furnished as Exhibit 99.1. They provide attributed supporting claims and do not override the 10-Qs. Their statements of operations repeat the 10-Q numbers, so they are not independent corroboration.

- Release Q3 (page:1 "ESCO REPORTS THIRD QUARTER FISCAL 2026 RESULTS"): segment EBIT, adjusted EBIT, EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA reconciliation (pages:6 to 8), balance sheet and cash flow (pages:8 to 9), backlog and orders (page:9), guidance and Megger status (page:3 "All filings for regulatory approval are underway and we continue to anticipate closing on the transaction in Q1 of fiscal 2027."). Non-GAAP definitions are on page:4. The adjusted interest line differs from the GAAP line (page:7), and the release footnotes list "$0.20 of debt financing" among the excluded items (page:6).

- Release Q2 (page:1 "ESCO REPORTS SECOND QUARTER FISCAL 2026 RESULTS", dated May 7, 2026) and Release Q1 (page:1 "ST. LOUIS, February 5, 2026"; the filename date 2026-01-30 is not the release date; the filename was not used to infer the period).
- Version note: guidance moved across releases (Release Q2 page:3 and Release Q3 page:3 each restate earlier ranges). Each release is a dated statement and does not revise an earlier one.
### Information-availability boundary

- Latest supplied documents: Release Q3 dated August 6, 2026 and 10-Q Q3 dated August 10, 2026. The cutoff is 2026-11-05. Nothing from August 11, 2026 to the cutoff is supplied. - No FY2026 10-K is supplied (the fiscal year ends September 30). With that year end, the first quarter of fiscal 2027 begins October 1, 2026, which is before the as-of date, so the expected closing window had opened by then.
### Identity and perimeter

- Reporting entity: ESCO Technologies Inc., a Missouri corporation (10-Q Q3 page:1 "ESCO TECHNOLOGIES INC."; 10-K page:56 "(a Missouri corporation)"), consolidated with subsidiaries. The 10-K states the credit facility is guaranteed by material US subsidiaries (page:80). No separate issuer, co-issuer or unrestricted-subsidiary distinction is printed; the registrant is the borrower together with "certain of its subsidiaries" (10-Q Q3 page:12).

- Debt roles: the Existing Credit Facility is led by JP Morgan Chase Bank, N.A. as administrative agent (10-Q Q3 page:10). The New Credit Facility is with the same administrative agent (page:12). No bonds or notes are identified in the debt tables (10-Q Q3 page:10 shows only a revolver and an incremental term loan A).

- Acquisition parties: the seller is TBG AG, the target is Megger Group Limited (10-Q Q3 page:19). A shareholder agreement with TBG AG is "to be executed concurrently with completion" (page:30). Its terms are not supplied.
- Discontinued operations: VACCO Industries was sold in July 2025 (10-K page:8). Net cash from discontinued operations is shown separately in the cash flows (10-K page:59; 10-Q Q3 page:3).

| CP-5 | Traceable claims, consistency across modules | All sources have page locators | Extraction fidelity unreviewed; no slides, HTML or XBRL |
### Document conflicts and consistency checks

- Contract liabilities: 10-Q Q3 page:16 states "contract assets, contract liabilities and accounts receivable totaled $127.6 million, $293.4 million and $267.5 million, respectively", while the balance sheet (page:3) prints contract liabilities of 288,142 (thousands). The same pattern appears at September 30, 2025: the 10-K balance sheet (page:58) prints 216,590 while the 10-Q Q3 note (page:16) gives "$224.7 million". The filings do not explain the difference on the pages opened. Downstream effect: CP-1 must not use the note figure and the balance sheet line interchangeably.

- Availability: the stated availability figures are not all on one basis. The 10-Q Q1 states availability "excluding the Incremental Facility" (page:19), while the 10-Q Q3 states "approximately $442 million available to borrow under the Existing Credit Facility" (page:11). Downstream effect: CP-2 must compute liquidity by facility from the printed inputs, not splice the stated availability figures across quarters.

- Interest: the 10-Q Q3 labels the caption "Interest expense, net" (page:2) and the release labels it "Interest expense" (Release Q3 page:5). The amounts shown for the quarter match. Downstream effect: label only; no amount conflict found on those pages.

- Balance sheet captions: the release prints one "Other current liabilities" line (Release Q3 page:8) where the 10-Q prints accrued salaries and accrued other expenses separately (page:3). Whether the release line is the sum of those two captions is not stated; the 10-Q controls the caption detail.

- Usable coverage: the 10-K plus three 10-Qs give an audited year and three consecutive unaudited quarters with comparatives on one perimeter (continuing operations after the VACCO sale), so a last-twelve-months view can be built from printed periods by downstream modules. Segment data is printed by quarter and nine months.

- Strongest contrary evidence: the Existing Credit Facility is to be replaced when the Megger acquisition completes, per the 10-Q Q3 page:12 text quoted above, and the acquisition is described as "total consideration of approximately $2.35 billion, consisting of $0.9 billion in cash and ESCO equity valued at approximately $1.4 billion" (page:19). The newest balance sheet therefore describes a capital structure that management expects to change when the acquisition closes, expected in the first quarter of fiscal 2027.

- Source risk mechanism: the filings print the sizes and tenors of the New Credit Facility but not its pricing, covenant definitions, conditions, or the Megger target's earnings. A consumer that reads only the June 30, 2026 debt table will understate the post-closing debt and cannot test post-closing leverage or interest coverage. The existing facility's covenant levels are also unprinted, so even the present headroom is not sourceable.

- Evidence to downstream consequence: CP-2 can describe facility-level debt, availability, letters of credit, lease obligations and the stated covenant types, and must mark headroom and pro forma leverage Not supplied. CP-1A can describe the transaction as management summarises it and must not state terms that sit only in the unsupplied agreements.
- What cannot proceed: covenant headroom on agreement definitions; pro forma leverage or coverage; Megger standalone analysis; any statement about events after August 10, 2026.

- Next evidence action: supply the Form 8-Ks of April 15, April 16 and June 3, 2026 with their exhibits (the share purchase agreement, the shareholder agreement and the May 29, 2026 credit agreement), the Amended and Restated Credit Agreement of August 30, 2023 with Amendment No. 1, any Megger financial statements or pro forma information, and any filing between August 11, 2026 and the cutoff.
### Coverage accounting

The remaining pages of the 10-K (89 pages), the 10-Q Q1 (24 pages), the 10-Q Q2 (28 pages), Release Q1 (8 pages) and Release Q2 (9 pages) are retained but were located by search only, not read in full. They are not claimed as inspected. Source quality and extraction status are kept apart: the text was extracted successfully, but no fidelity review against the filed HTML was done.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| On reported figures ESCO has low leverage and strong cash conversion, with total debt of $85.0 million at June 30, 2026. That base excludes the Megger acquisition, which management expects to close in the first quarter of fiscal 2027. | Medium | Pro forma debt, covenant levels and Megger earnings are not supplied, so the reported base may not describe the post-closing company. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Total debt fell from $186.0 million at September 30, 2025 to $85.0 million at June 30, 2026, and LTM EBITDA of $305.7 million gives total debt to EBITDA of 0.278x. | Reported leverage is very low and net debt is small, giving headroom before the acquisition financing. | High |

| Operating cash flow from continuing operations was $193.4 million for the nine months to June 30, 2026, against $88.3 million a year earlier, helped by contract liability growth. | Cash generation is strong but part reflects customer advances timing, so it may not repeat. | Medium |

| Liquidity at June 30, 2026 is $73.2 million of cash plus $442.3 million of undrawn revolver after letters of credit. | Near-term liquidity is ample and no maturity falls before August 30, 2028 except $20.0 million due within twelve months. | High |

| The $2.35 billion Megger purchase includes $0.9 billion in cash, and new facilities of $500 million each (revolver, term loan A, term loan B) are committed but not yet effective. | Debt is expected to rise materially at closing, so the current low leverage is temporary. | Medium |

| Nine-month cash flow from continuing operations excludes a discontinued-operations outflow of $59.3 million, alongside approximately $59 million of tax paid on the VACCO gain. | Free cash flow from continuing operations overstates cash available after that one-off tax. | Medium |
### Financial base view

On reported figures, ESCO enters the Megger transaction from a strong and lightly levered base. Total borrowings at June 30, 2026 were $85.0 million against LTM EBITDA of $305.677 million, and cash was $73.236 million, so net debt was $11.764 million. Over the same twelve months EBITDA covered cash interest paid about twenty times. Liquidity of $515.536 million is mostly an undrawn $500 million revolver. These are reported-basis ratios computed here, not covenant ratios, because the credit agreement definitions are not supplied.

In US$ millions, the headline figures are: total borrowings of $186.0 million at September 30, 2025 and $85.0 million at June 30, 2026; LTM EBITDA of $305.7 million; operating cash flow from continuing operations of $193.4 million for the nine months to June 30, 2026 against $88.3 million for the prior-year nine months; cash of $73.2 million and undrawn revolver of $442.3 million at June 30, 2026; a current portion of debt of $20.0 million; and a discontinued-operations operating outflow of $59.3 million.

Three features limit how far this base can be used. First, it is a pre-acquisition picture. The signed Megger purchase (approximately $2.35 billion, of which $0.9 billion is cash) is to be financed by a new $1.5 billion committed facility set that will replace the existing facility at closing, so the debt table at June 30, 2026 describes a structure management expects to retire. Second, the LTM period carries the Maritime acquisition (closed April 25, 2025) for all four quarters, but FY2025 and 9M 2025 carry it only from that date, so year-on-year growth includes acquired revenue, and the latest nine months include a large working capital inflow and a large discontinued-operations outflow, so LTM cash conversion is not a clean run rate. Third, the 10-Q Q3 prints nine-month cash flows only, so discrete Q3 cash flow is not available.

The statements are consistent with each other where checked: the 10-K and the 10-Q Q3 print the same September 30, 2025 total assets, and the release quarterly EBITDA figures sum to the nine-month figure (see Calculations). The status for downstream use is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS: CP-1A and CP-2 can use the figures below; CP-2 must treat covenant headroom and post-closing leverage as Not supplied.

In Q2 2026 the Company paid approximately $59 million of cash taxes on the gain (10-Q Q3 page:25), shown in discontinued operations cash flow of (59,340) for the nine months (10-Q Q3 page:3).

### Definition review
| Definition | Source | Treatment here |
| EBIT | Release Q3 page:4 "The Company defines “EBIT” as earnings before interest and taxes" | Used as EBT plus interest expense, net; ties to 10-Q Q3 page:23 |

| EBITDA | Release Q3 page:4, earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization | EBIT plus D&A from the cash flow statement; matches the release quarterly "Consolidated EBITDA" for Q1, Q2, Q3 and the nine months |

| Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBIT | Release Q3 page:4, excluding items in the reconciliation | Not used in ratios; adjusted EBIT excludes acquisition-related amortization, restructuring, Megger financing and acquisition costs; LTM adjusted EBITDA is Not calculable because the FY2025 adjusted figure is not supplied |
| Total debt | 10-Q Q3 page:10 "Total borrowings" | Revolver plus term loan A; excludes leases and letters of credit |
| Interest paid | Cash flow supplemental line | Used as cash interest; not split by continuing and discontinued operations |
| Covenant leverage and interest coverage | 10-K page:80 | Definitions Not supplied |
### Narrative review
#### Leverage

On the reported basis, leverage is low and falling: total debt to EBITDA of 0.758x at FY2025 compares with 0.278x for the LTM to June 30, 2026, with total borrowings down 101,000 (thousands) from 186,000 to 85,000 over nine months. The mechanism was operating cash flow from continuing operations of 193,377 funding net repayment of 101,000 (231,000 repaid less 130,000 borrowed), the 59,340 discontinued-operations outflow, capital spending and dividends (10-Q Q3 pages:3 and 4). The credit implication is limited headroom risk today, but the May 29, 2026 agreement and the equity-and-cash purchase price mean the position is expected to change. Illustrative sensitivity only: if the full $0.9 billion cash consideration were borrowed on top of current debt, total debt would be about 3.22x LTM ESCO-only EBITDA before Megger earnings, fees and any cash used. This is a bound on method, not a forecast, and Megger EBITDA is Not supplied.
#### Coverage

Cash interest cover is about twenty times on LTM figures. The 10-Q Q3 cites "lower average outstanding borrowings" and "lower average interest rates" as partial offsets to the higher interest expense (page:23), which is consistent with the low cash interest in the denominator. Cover on interest expense, net is lower because Q3 2026 includes about 7 million of financing costs; on that basis LTM EBITDA is 15.99 times the 19,121 charge (see Calculations). Post-closing interest on up to $1.5 billion of committed term and revolver capacity is Not supplied.
#### Cash flow quality

Continuing operations produced 193,377 of operating cash flow in nine months against 88,299, an increase that the 10-Q Q3 attributes to "lower working capital requirements and higher earnings" (page:24). Contract liabilities rose 71.5 million "due to timing of payments received from customers" (page:24), which is customer advance timing that can reverse. Discontinued operations used 59,340, largely VACCO gain tax, so total operating cash flow was 134,037. Free cash flow of 258,102 for the LTM period is therefore a continuing-operations figure before that one-time tax and before dividends; it should not be read as the cash available after all outflows.
#### Liquidity

Liquidity at June 30, 2026 is 515.536 (US$m): cash 73.236 and undrawn revolver 442.300 after 12.7 of letters of credit. The Existing Credit Facility runs to August 30, 2028 with no maturity in the next twelve months other than the 20.0 current portion. Cash fell from 101.350 at September 30, 2025 as debt was repaid. Liquidity after closing depends on the New Credit Facility, which is not effective and not supplied beyond its sizes.
#### Data quality

Statements are tied: segment profit reconciles to EBT (10-Q Q3 pages:8 and 9), the 10-K and 10-Q Q3 print the same September 30, 2025 total assets, and the release quarterly EBITDA sums to the nine-month figure. Open points are the contract-liabilities note against the balance sheet caption (10-Q Q3 page:16 "$293.4 million" against 288,142 on page:3, unexplained), Release Q3 printing "Interest expense" where the 10-Q prints "Interest expense, net" (same amount), and the release's single "Other current liabilities" line. No restatement notice appears in the supplied filings other than the VACCO recast.
#### Definition risks

The agreement's leverage and coverage definitions are Not supplied, so no reported ratio here is a covenant ratio. Release adjusted measures exclude acquisition amortization and deal costs, and adjusted EBITDA is not a lender definition. Net debt here excludes finance and operating leases. Including finance leases alone the LTM leverage is 0.328x, and including operating leases as well 0.493x (see Calculations).
#### Key gaps

Covenant levels and ratios; the New Credit Facility terms; Megger financials; pro forma debt and interest; the repayment schedule of term loan A; discrete Q3 cash flow; June 30, 2025 debt (needed for a 9M 2025 balance column); pension and retiree medical; and anything after August 10, 2026.
### Downstream readiness

| LTM EBITDA of 305,677 | Yes | Calculated | Components all located; not a reported figure |

| Covenant headroom | Yes | Insufficient Information | Levels not supplied |
| Illustrative 3.22x with full cash consideration borrowed | Yes | Analyst Inference | Assumption: all $0.9 billion borrowed, no cash used, Megger EBITDA omitted |
## Calculations
All inputs are US$ thousands as printed, with locators in the tables above. No input was replaced with zero.
### EBIT and EBITDA
- EBIT = earnings before income taxes + interest expense, net.
- Checks: FY2024 and FY2025 equal segment profit after corporate on 10-K page:85 (146,200 and 170,355); 9M figures equal EBIT on 10-Q Q3 page:23.
- EBITDA = EBIT + D&A (cash flow statement; continuing operations because the same statement removes discontinued earnings before adding D&A).
- Checks against Release Q3 page:7: 214,361 and 154,060 match.
- LTM = FY2025 + 9M 2026 - 9M 2025, for every flow row.

- LTM at December 31, 2025: 245,376 + 64,851 - 41,025 = 269,202. LTM at March 31, 2026: 245,376 + 137,951 - 90,710 = 292,617 (six-month EBITDA from Release Q2 page:7 and its comparative; Q1 2026 EBITDA 64,851 and Q1 2025 EBITDA 41,025 from Release Q1 page:6).
### Free cash flow
- FCF = net cash from operating activities, continuing operations - capital expenditures - additions to capitalized software and other, before dividends and acquisitions.
- Total operating cash flow 9M 2026 = 193,377 + (59,340 outflow) = 134,037, which equals the printed figure (10-Q Q3 page:3).
### Leverage, net debt and cover
- EBITDA / interest expense, net, LTM: 305,677 / 19,121 = 15.99x.

- Illustrative sensitivity (not pro forma): (85,000 + 900,000) / 305,677 = 3.22x. Inputs: June 30, 2026 borrowings plus the $0.9 billion cash consideration from 10-Q Q3 page:19, assuming it is all borrowed, no cash is used, fees are nil and Megger EBITDA is zero. It overstates leverage by omitting Megger EBITDA and understates it by omitting fees and any other costs.
### Liquidity

- Undrawn revolver = commitment 500,000 - drawn - letters of credit. September 30, 2025: 500,000 - 25,000 - 10,100 = 464,900. December 31, 2025: 500,000 - 20,511 - 10,700 = 468,789 (the 20,511 is revolver plus short-term borrowings as printed). March 31, 2026: 500,000 - 45,000 - 14,500 = 440,500. June 30, 2026: 500,000 - 45,000 - 12,700 = 442,300.
- Implied Q4 2025 (September 30, 2025 quarter) net sales = 1,095,388 - 742,714 = 352,674 and EBITDA = 245,376 - 154,060 = 91,316, shown only to explain the LTM bridge.

## Next module

- CP-1A: carry the Megger transaction (signed April 15, 2026; approximately $2.35 billion; $0.9 billion cash and equity valued at about $1.4 billion; expected closing first quarter of fiscal 2027; New Credit Facility of $1.5 billion in three tranches, effective only at closing) and treat all terms beyond the 10-Q Q3 summary as Not supplied. Keep the VACCO and Maritime history on the continuing-operations perimeter.

### Reader summary

| Three segments serve aerospace and defense, electric utilities and RF testing; the US Government accounted for approximately 23% of fiscal 2025 revenue and no customer exceeded 10%. | Spread across segments, but defense budget and program timing risk is concentrated in aerospace and defense. | High |

### Business and transaction view

ESCO is a publicly listed group with no sponsor or parent named in the context or the filings; material US subsidiaries guarantee the bank facility (10-K page:80). It reports three segments: Aerospace & Defense (A&D), Utility Solutions Group (USG) and RF Test & Measurement (Test). A&D has grown from 34% of continuing revenue in 2023 to 44% in 2025, reflecting Navy growth and the Maritime acquisition, which makes the group more dependent on US and UK naval programs and on government funding. The group sold its Space business (VACCO) in July 2025 and used the proceeds mainly to repay debt, so fiscal 2025 and the first nine months of fiscal 2026 show deleveraging rather than distributions.

The transaction that matters is the pending purchase of Megger Group Limited from TBG AG, signed April 15, 2026, with total consideration of approximately $2.35 billion, of which approximately $0.9 billion is cash and approximately $1.4 billion is ESCO equity. Megger, which the 10-K lists as a competitor of the USG segment, will join USG. The cash part is to be funded from cash and incremental debt, with a new $1.5 billion committed facility set agreed on May 29, 2026 that is effective only on closing. Closing was expected in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, which began October 1, 2026, so by the 2026-11-05 as-of date the transaction may have closed. No supplied source is dated after August 10, 2026, so closing status, the debt actually drawn and the size of TBG AG's resulting stake are Not supplied.

For a creditor the view is that the operating base is diversified and well covered by backlog, but the credit story is now event driven. The equity component limits the cash leverage needed, yet it creates a new significant shareholder whose agreement terms are unknown, and Megger's earnings and its effect on leverage are Not supplied. Evidence quality is High for ESCO's own filed facts and Low for anything about Megger beyond the purchase terms summarised in the 10-Q Q3.

| Pricing and margin | Segment commentary cites price increases and volume leverage, offset by inflation | Release Q3 page:2 "driven by leverage on higher volume and price increases, partially offset by inflationary pressures and unfavorable mix" | Management Language | Management attribution; margin durability not independently tested here |

| Capital spending and working capital | Capital spending and software investment are modest relative to operating cash flow; working capital swings with contract billings | CP-1 financial base; 10-Q Q3 page:24 "Contract liabilities increased $71.5 million primarily within the A&D segment (Globe and Maritime) due to timing of payments received from customers." | Analyst Interpretation | Customer advances flatter operating cash flow and can reverse |

| Business model risk | Government funding risk is named first in the risk factors | 10-K page:17 "Restrictions in authorized U.S. Government defense spending or changes in acquisition priorities could negatively impact our financial position and result of operations." | Documentary Fact | A budget shock would hit A&D, the largest and fastest-growing segment |
### Company profile
| Attribute | Value | Evidence and locator | Category |
| Legal name and ticker | ESCO Technologies Inc., NYSE: ESE | 10-Q Q3 page:1 "ESCO TECHNOLOGIES INC." | Documentary Fact |
| Country and incorporation | United States; incorporated in Missouri; headquartered in St. Louis, Missouri | 10-K page:1 "Missouri"; 10-K page:1 "St. Louis, Missouri" | Documentary Fact |

| Sector | Context label "Communications Equipment, NEC"; the filings describe aerospace and defense, utility diagnostics and RF test, so the label is a classification code, not a business description | context; 10-K page:5 "A global provider of highly engineered components and systems for aviation, Navy, defense and industrial customers" | Analyst Interpretation |
| Fiscal year end | September 30 | 10-K page:6 | Documentary Fact |

Tucker, SVP and CFO since April 2021 | 10-K pages:16 to 17 "President and Chief Executive Officer since January 1, 2023"; "Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer since April 2021" | Documentary Fact |

| Auditor | Grant Thornton LLP, auditor since 2021; unqualified opinion on FY2025 statements; ICFR opinion excludes Maritime | 10-K page:55 "We have served as the Company’s auditor since 2021."; 10-K page:56 | Documentary Fact |

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The pending transaction is the acquisition of Megger Group Limited from TBG AG. On April 15, 2026 ESCO signed a definitive agreement: 10-Q Q3 page:19 states "ESCO will acquire Megger for total consideration of approximately $2.35 billion, consisting of $0.9 billion in cash and ESCO equity valued at approximately $1.4 billion." The agreement is a share purchase agreement (10-Q Q3 page:30 "for the sale and purchase of the share capital of Megger Group Limited") with a Form of Shareholder Agreement to be executed concurrently with completion. The cash and equity components are each stated as approximate and do not sum to the stated total; the filing does not explain the difference, and it is logged below, not reconciled.

Status and timing. The transaction was signed after the March 31, 2026 balance sheet date and was reported as a "Subsequent Event" in the 10-Q Q2 (page:24). Management states that "All filings for regulatory approval are underway" and expects closing in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 (Release Q3 page:3 and 10-Q Q3 page:19). Whether approvals were received and whether it has closed by 2026-11-05 is Not supplied.

Financing and new debt. The cash portion "will be funded through existing cash on hand and incremental debt, with committed financing in place" (10-Q Q3 page:19). On May 29, 2026 ESCO and certain subsidiaries entered into a Credit Agreement, the New Credit Facility, with JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as administrative agent. It provides a senior secured revolving credit facility of $500 million, a senior secured term loan A of $500 million and a senior secured term loan B of $500 million. It becomes effective only on, and substantially concurrently with, closing and replaces the Existing Credit Facility. The revolver and term loan A mature five years after the effective date and term loan B seven years after (10-Q Q3 page:12). Foreign subsidiaries may also draw. No notes, bonds or other capital-markets debt issue is described in any supplied source. The credit agreement is Exhibit 10.3 to the 10-Q Q3 and was filed with the Form 8-K of June 3, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:30); it is not in the pack, so pricing, covenants, conditions to effectiveness, guarantors and collateral are Not supplied.

Ownership effect. The equity component means ESCO will issue shares to TBG AG at completion. The number of shares, the resulting percentage ownership, lock-up terms, board or consent rights and any standstill under the shareholder agreement are all Not supplied. No percentage is inferred here.

Use of proceeds and liquidity effect. Proceeds fund the purchase price; fees, expenses and any refinancing of the Existing Credit Facility are not itemised in the supplied sources. CP-1 shows $85.0 million of borrowings and $73.2 million of cash at June 30, 2026 before the transaction, and an illustrative bound of 3.22x on ESCO-only EBITDA if the full $0.9 billion were borrowed (CP-1, Analyst Inference, not a forecast). Megger financials are Not supplied, so the actual pro forma leverage and liquidity cannot be stated.

Costs already incurred. Approximately $7 million of debt financing costs were expensed in Q3 2026 interest expense (10-Q Q3 page:23), and acquisition costs at Corporate are excluded from adjusted EPS (Release Q3 page:6 "$0.20 of debt financing and $0.19 of acquisition costs"). These are Documentary Fact; they show the financing was committed before the 10-Q Q3 period end.

Creditor mechanics. A large acquisition funded partly by new term debt replaces an $85.0 million drawn facility with up to $1.5 billion of committed capacity (three tranches of $500 million, see Calculations). The creditor question is leverage tolerance, covenant terms and the term loan B tenor. Willingness is evidenced by the committed financing and the signed agreement; legal capacity (what the new agreement permits) and feasibility (post-closing cash flow of the combined group) are not shown.

Earlier financing for context: the Maritime acquisition in April 2025 for a cash purchase price of approximately $472 million, net of cash acquired (10-K page:74), was partly funded by the Incremental Facility (10-K page:80), which is the term loan A now outstanding.

## Calculations

One simple sum: the New Credit Facility commitments are $500 million + $500 million + $500 million = $1.5 billion (10-Q Q3 page:12). Otherwise CP-1A does not compute figures. Every other number is quoted from a located source or taken unchanged from CP-1, with the period each source gives. Also checked: the stated Megger components $0.9 billion + $1.4 billion = $2.3 billion, against the stated total of approximately $2.35 billion (see Conflicts). The only derived item mentioned, the 3.22x illustrative bound, is CP-1's own calculation (CP-1 Calculations: 85,000 + 900,000 = 985,000 divided by LTM EBITDA of 305,677), and it is labelled Analyst Inference there.

spans.text: # CP-2 fundamental credit synthesis: ESCO TECHNOLOGIES INC (ese)
## Request

ESCO TECHNOLOGIES INC (issuer id `ese`) is assessed as of 2026-11-05 on the `credit_snapshot` pathway. The scope is the fundamental credit view built only from the CP-0, CP-1 and CP-1A handoffs, with no source text re-read and no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.
## Sources
CP-2 works from upstream handoffs only. The issuer sources below are the files those handoffs rely on; this module did not reopen them, and every figure and fact here traces to CP-1 or CP-1A.
### Issuer sources relied on (through the handoffs)
| Source (exact name) | sha256 |
| 10-K_2025-09-30_ese-20250930x10k.htm.jsonl | fe80d5d10f35aaa7f1b7aa40e6d69aeaea7f501fabdde619947c03aa0fe69d71 |
### Other inputs
| Input | sha256 |
| context (`contexts/866706-esco-technologies-inc-ese.json`; run settings, not issuer evidence) | da65696ce609dcf19999b44c58b8a10f43f7d7bc7cde7c4a3762d76affdde214 |
### Supplied handoffs
| Module | sha256 | Use |
| CP-0 | 7f46d3b1dbdad4b468a5bdd5db37f408dc8a1ce57aba77ff195a116822899d17 | Source readiness: READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS; gap list |
| CP-1 | 23a50d14b3104c2571d80147c88f81427457a9b11a2aa773f3459c4d026de1e7 | Financial base: leverage, cover, liquidity, maturities, claims outside debt |
| CP-1A | 7bb2aa7585c6ae63abcfb32f227dd60a79e423f35bf4601e20c348a72e1bc24b | Business, transaction, governance, conflicts, consumer judgments |
### Basis labels

Bracketed basis labels name the upstream section: CP-1 sections are "Chart data", "Financials and credit metrics", "Debt instruments and facilities", "Claims outside debt", "Covenants and definitions" and "Narrative review"; CP-1A sections are "Company and operating model", "Company profile", "Transaction summary and new debt issues", "Ownership, governance and sponsor behaviour", "Timeline", "Conflicts and document differences" and "Credit translations". Periods follow the fiscal year ending September 30: Q3 2026 is the quarter ended June 30, 2026, LTM is the twelve months to June 30, 2026. Currency is USD.

CP-2 consistency: this module carries the CP-1 and CP-1A figures unchanged and corrects neither. It repeats CP-1A's two logged conflicts (Megger consideration components; the wording of the current portion of debt) as limits on the maturity and transaction reading, without resolving them.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| ESCO is lightly levered today, with USD 85.0 million of borrowings and USD 515.536 million of liquidity at June 30, 2026, but the pending Megger acquisition will reset debt, covenants and ownership. | Medium | Covenant levels, the new credit agreement, Megger financials and anything after August 10, 2026 are not supplied, so the post-closing credit cannot be sized. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Total debt to EBITDA was 0.278x and EBITDA covered cash interest 20.42x on a last-twelve-months basis to June 30, 2026. | Reported leverage and debt service capacity are strong before the acquisition financing. | High |

| Liquidity of USD 515.536 million is mostly an undrawn revolver, and only USD 20.000 million of debt falls due within twelve months. | Near-term refinancing and liquidity risk is low until the existing facility is replaced. | High |

| Backlog of USD 1,540.5 million and a diversified three-segment base support revenue, but the US Government is approximately 23% of revenue and contracts can be terminated for convenience. | Revenue is visible but exposed to defense budget and program timing in the largest segment. | Medium |

| The Megger purchase is approximately USD 2.35 billion, of which USD 0.9 billion is cash, funded with new term loans and a revolver of USD 500 million each. | Leverage and covenant terms will change at closing and cannot yet be tested. | Medium |

| Documented behaviour since fiscal 2025 is supportive of creditors, with debt repaid after the VACCO sale and no buybacks. | Past conduct is a positive signal, but post-closing behaviour and TBG AG's rights are unknown. | Medium |
### Credit view

ESCO Technologies currently has a strong, lightly levered credit profile, but the credit view depends on a pending acquisition that this evidence cannot size. At June 30, 2026 ESCO had USD 85.0 million of borrowings against LTM EBITDA of USD 305.677 million (total debt 0.278x, net debt 0.038x), liquidity of USD 515.536 million and backlog of USD 1,540.5 million [CP-1; CP-1A Company and operating model]. The weakest point is that this describes ESCO before the Megger purchase, which includes USD 0.9 billion of cash funded under new facilities whose terms, and Megger's own earnings, are not supplied [CP-1A Transaction summary]. What decides the outcome is whether closing has occurred, how much is drawn on the new term loans and what the covenants allow.
Confidence is Medium, not High, because CP-1A judged CP-2 ready only with limitations (see Gaps) and the covenant and transaction documents are missing.
### Key findings

ESCO has very low reported leverage and strong cover. Total borrowings were USD 85.0 million at June 30, 2026, down from USD 186.0 million at September 30, 2025, so total debt to EBITDA fell from 0.758x to 0.278x and net debt to EBITDA from 0.345x to 0.038x. EBITDA covered cash interest paid 20.42x on an LTM basis against 14.09x for FY2025 [CP-1 Chart data]. The mechanism was operating cash flow from continuing operations of USD 193.377 million in nine months 2026 funding net repayment and other uses, so the debt reduction came from cash generation, which supports debt service capacity [CP-1 Narrative review: leverage].

ESCO has ample liquidity and a short near-term maturity profile. Cash was USD 73.236 million and the revolver had USD 442.300 million undrawn after USD 12.7 million of letters of credit, together USD 515.536 million; USD 20.000 million of term loan A is current and USD 65.000 million falls due by August 30, 2028, which is the maturity of the existing revolver and term loan A [CP-1 Chart data]. The existing facility is secured by guarantees from material US subsidiaries and a pledge of equity of material foreign subsidiaries [CP-1 Debt instruments and facilities]. Because the facility is to be replaced at the Megger closing, this maturity profile is a pre-closing picture. The wording of the current portion changed from voluntary in Q1 2026 to obligated in Q2 and Q3 2026, a logged conflict the supplied documents do not explain [CP-1A Conflicts].

ESCO has diversified operations with a government-weighted core. Aerospace & Defense was approximately 44% of fiscal 2025 revenue, Utility Solutions Group approximately 35% and RF Test approximately 21%; the US Government and its contractors were approximately 23%, and no customer exceeded 10% [CP-1A Company and operating model]. Backlog of USD 1,540.5 million, with approximately 59% expected in the next twelve months, gives revenue visibility, but Government contracts are terminable for convenience and fixed-price contracts expose margins to cost overruns [CP-1A Credit translations].

ESCO's cash flow in the latest nine months may overstate a normal level. Continuing operating cash flow of USD 193.377 million benefited from customer advances, with contract liabilities up USD 71.5 million, and discontinued operations used USD 59.340 million, alongside approximately USD 59 million of cash tax paid on the VACCO gain. LTM free cash flow of USD 258.102 million is therefore a continuing-operations figure before that one-time outflow and before dividends [CP-1 Narrative review: cash flow quality]. Customer advances can reverse as projects deliver, which would lower operating cash flow.

ESCO's acquisition will change the credit. The Megger purchase has total consideration of approximately USD 2.35 billion, of which USD 0.9 billion is cash and approximately USD 1.4 billion is ESCO equity, with closing expected in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 [CP-1A Transaction summary]. Committed financing is a new senior secured revolver, term loan A and term loan B of USD 500 million each, effective only at closing and replacing the existing facility [CP-1 Debt instruments and facilities]. Megger's financials are not supplied, so post-closing leverage and cover are not calculable. As a bound only, CP-1 shows that if the full USD 0.9 billion cash consideration were borrowed on top of current debt, total debt would be about 3.22x ESCO-only LTM EBITDA before Megger earnings; this is an Analyst Inference, not a forecast [CP-1 Narrative review: leverage]. The 2026-11-05 as-of date falls after the start of the expected closing quarter, and nothing after August 10, 2026 is supplied, so closing status is unknown.

ESCO's covenants cannot be tested. The existing facility has a leverage ratio and an interest coverage ratio, and management reported compliance at June 30, 2026, but levels, definitions and the reported ratios are not supplied, and the New Credit Facility terms are not supplied [CP-1 Covenants and definitions]. Headroom is therefore not calculable, and the reported ratios in this credit view are not covenant ratios.

ESCO's observed conduct supports creditors, and ownership will change. VACCO proceeds were used mainly to pay down debt, dividends are small, there were no buybacks in fiscal 2025 or Q3 2026 and no creditor-adverse action appears in the supplied sources. TBG AG will receive ESCO shares and sign a shareholder agreement at completion; its stake, governance rights and lock-up terms are not supplied [CP-1A Ownership, governance and sponsor behaviour].
### Strengths and weaknesses

ESCO's strengths start with its balance sheet. Reported leverage is low (total debt to EBITDA 0.278x) and cash interest cover is high (20.42x) on LTM figures, giving the issuer capacity to absorb a cost or volume shock before the acquisition financing [CP-1 Chart data; Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation]. Liquidity of USD 515.536 million is dominated by an undrawn revolver that matures August 30, 2028, so near-term refinancing risk is low [CP-1 Chart data; Documentary Fact]. Backlog of USD 1,540.5 million and a three-segment mix with no customer above 10% of sales support revenue visibility and limit single-customer risk [CP-1A Company and operating model; Documentary Fact]. Capital allocation since fiscal 2025 has favoured creditors, with debt repaid from divestiture proceeds, small dividends and no buybacks [CP-1A Ownership, governance and sponsor behaviour; Documentary Fact]. Cash generation from continuing operations was strong in the latest period [CP-1 Narrative review; Documentary Fact, qualified by working capital timing].

ESCO's weaknesses concentrate on the pending transaction and on missing documents. The Megger purchase is large relative to the existing debt, is funded partly with new term debt, and its terms and Megger's earnings are not supplied, so the leverage that creditors will face is unknown [CP-1A Transaction summary; Insufficient Information, with the missing datapoints being the credit agreement, Megger financials and closing status]. Covenant levels and headroom are missing for both the existing and the new facility [CP-1 Covenants and definitions; Insufficient Information]. Government funding concentration in Aerospace & Defense, termination for convenience and fixed-price cost risk could affect the largest and fastest-growing segment [CP-1A Credit translations; Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation]. Operating cash flow was lifted by customer advances and the reported free cash flow excludes a discontinued-operations outflow, so cash conversion is flattered in the nine months [CP-1 Narrative review: cash flow quality; Analyst Interpretation]. TBG AG's resulting stake and governance rights are unknown, which limits the view of control and alignment after closing [CP-1A Ownership, governance and sponsor behaviour; Insufficient Information]. Smaller weaknesses are renewables exposure in the utility segment, sole-source suppliers, and internal-control scope that excludes recently acquired businesses until they are tested [CP-1A Company and operating model; Documentary Fact].
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity | Basis |

| Acquisition financing and leverage step-up | Cash consideration of USD 0.9 billion is funded from cash and new term loans effective at closing | Debt rises from USD 85.0 million to a level that depends on draws; leverage tolerance and debt service capacity are untested | Material | CP-1 Debt instruments; CP-1A Transaction summary |

| Covenant and documentation opacity | Leverage and coverage tests exist but levels and definitions are not supplied | Headroom and restricted payment capacity cannot be assessed; monitoring posture is limited | Material | CP-1 Covenants and definitions |

| Government funding and termination concentration | About 23% of revenue from the US Government, terminable for convenience; A&D is the largest segment | A budget or program shock reduces revenue in the segment that now carries most growth | Material | CP-1A Company and operating model |

| Cash flow reversal | Customer advances and a working capital inflow lifted operating cash flow | Normal cash conversion may be lower, reducing debt paydown capacity | Material | CP-1 Narrative review |

| Ownership and control change | Equity consideration issued to TBG AG with a shareholder agreement at completion | Governance rights and influence over distributions or further transactions are unknown | Material | CP-1A Ownership and governance |

| Refinancing and maturity reset | Existing facility replaced; new tenors of five and seven years; amounts drawn unknown | Maturity wall and amortisation cannot be built; current portion wording is unexplained | Material | CP-1 Chart data; CP-1A Conflicts |
| Fixed-price contract and margin risk | Cost overruns reduce margin on fixed-price work | Lower EBITDA cover if cost inflation persists | Minor | CP-1A Credit translations |

| Renewables and supplier concentration | NRG orders fell with tax credit expiry; sole-source components exist | Segment earnings and delivery timing could weaken | Minor | CP-1A Company and operating model |

| Integration and control scope | Maritime was excluded from the internal control audit scope at year end; Megger will be a further integration | Reporting risk during integration | Minor | CP-1A Ownership, governance and sponsor behaviour |
### Assessment
| Element | Content | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Fundamental credit view | Lightly levered with strong liquidity and cover today; event-driven by the pending Megger acquisition; post-closing credit not sizeable from supplied evidence | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 Chart data and Financials and credit metrics; CP-1A Transaction summary and Credit translations |

| Thesis | ESCO's strong liquidity, low reported leverage, backlog and creditor-supportive conduct support its credit today, while the unseen terms of the Megger financing, its covenants and its ownership change decide the credit once the acquisition closes | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1; CP-1A |
## Calculations

No new calculation. CP-2 carries the CP-1 figures unchanged: leverage, cover, liquidity and maturity figures come from CP-1 Chart data, the free cash flow from CP-1 Financials and credit metrics, and the 3.22x bound from CP-1 Calculations (an Analyst Inference there). The percentages for revenue by segment and for the US Government are CP-1A figures taken from the 10-K. Nothing here is recomputed or replaced with zero.
## Gaps

| Closing status and events after August 10, 2026 not supplied (CP-0, CP-1, CP-1A) | The as-of date is after the start of the expected closing quarter; debt may already be different | All conclusions | High | Supply later 8-Ks or confirm none |
| TBG AG stake, governance rights and lock-up not supplied (CP-1A) | Control and alignment after closing | Governance and ownership | High | Supply the shareholder agreement |

| Consideration components do not add to the stated total (CP-1A conflict, logged not reconciled) | Size of the transaction and equity issued is uncertain | Transaction reading | Medium | Obtain the April 15, 2026 8-K |

| Current portion of debt: wording changed from voluntary to obligated (CP-1A conflict, logged not reconciled) | Maturity and amortisation profile of term loan A | Maturity profile | Medium | Supply Amendment No. 1 and later amendments |
| Term loan A repayment schedule and fiscal-year maturity split not supplied (CP-1) | Maturity wall cannot be built beyond two buckets | Refinancing | Medium | Supply the credit agreement schedule |

| CP-1A judged CP-2 as ready with limitations, not ready (CP-1A Consumers) | Inherited signal: the synthesis must treat post-closing structure and ownership as Not supplied | Confidence capped below High | Medium | Resolve the High gaps above |
| Release adjusted EBITDA cannot be extended to LTM (FY2025 adjusted not supplied) (CP-1) | No adjusted leverage measure is available | Definitions | Medium | Supply the fiscal Q4 2025 release |
| Contract liabilities note and balance sheet caption differ (CP-0, CP-1) | Reading of customer advances and working capital | Cash flow quality | Medium | Locate the explanation in the filed HTML |

## Findings
### Reader summary

One statement on cash interest is unsupported, and covenant, new financing and Megger documents are missing, so committee use is restricted. | Low | Executed credit agreements, Megger documents and any filing after August 10, 2026 are not supplied, so legal terms and post-closing leverage cannot be traced. |

| No source after August 10, 2026 is supplied. | Closing status and drawn debt at the as-of date cannot be traced. | High |
### Evidence trace view

Overall, evidence traceability is Ready with Remediation. Of the Top 5 material credit drivers, 2 are directly sourced, 2 are calculated, 0 are assumption-based, 0 are analyst inferences, and 1 are weak-lineage, untraced, conflicting, or insufficient-information items. The most important provenance gap is the absence of the executed credit agreements (covenant levels and the New Credit Facility terms), which matters because covenant headroom and post-closing leverage cannot be traced to any source and implies that committee use must be restricted rather than approved.
This is consistent with the auditability assessment in the appendix, where the lowest dimension is Ready with Remediation.
### Traceability conclusion

The upstream modules are traceable enough for restricted committee use but not for a clean pass. Every figure behind the leverage, liquidity and cover conclusions was recomputed from the filed statements and matched, and each quoted passage was found on its cited page. The weakest point is that the most decision-relevant item, covenant headroom after the Megger financing, rests on documents that were never supplied, so the handoffs correctly mark it Not supplied rather than estimate it. One cover-ratio caveat in the financial base is unsupported and should be corrected or restated as unknown. What decides committee use is whether the executed credit agreements, the Megger documents and filings after August 10, 2026 are added; until then the credit view can be used only with those limits.
### Clearance decision
CLEARANCE DECISION: Pass with Remediation. Critical Issues: 0. Material Issues: 1. Minor Issues: 12. Committee Use: Restricted.

No Critical finding exists, so the grade is not Blocked, but one Material finding (CP5-001, an unsupported statement about cash interest in the financial base) and the missing executed legal documents keep committee use restricted. The research QA status is Restricted. Under the confidence rule that a Restricted status caps the score at 59, the band is Low. The Material issue must be disclosed with any committee use of the cover ratio.
### Remediation priority map
1. Must-fix before committee: CP5-001. Restate the LTM cash interest cover caveat as unknown, or show the cover on both bases, and disclose it with the 20.42x figure.

2. Must-fix before the handoff is consumed downstream: CP5-002 and CP5-013. Keep the 3.22x bound labelled as an Analyst Inference with its omitted inputs wherever reused, and keep relative value, ratings and market data out of the credit view.

3. Monitoring follow-up: CP5-003, CP5-007, CP5-008, CP5-009 and CP5-010. Obtain the April 15, 2026 8-K, the executed credit agreements and the explanation for the contract-liability difference and the current-portion wording; re-audit when they arrive.

4. Formatting and hygiene: CP5-004, CP5-005, CP5-006, CP5-011 and CP5-012. Tighten three wordings (undrawn revolver description, segment growth statement, "will reset"), remove repeated caveats, and note the transport envelope.

## Calculations

The host recomputed every derived figure in the audited handoffs from located inputs. Inputs were re-read from the pinned text, and the key statement lines were also extracted by script and compared. All results are in USD thousands unless stated.

- Interest cover: 305,677 / 14,970 = 20.42x; 245,376 / 17,421 = 14.09x; 198,355 / 14,535 = 13.65x. LTM interest paid: 17,421 + 13,587 - 16,038 = 14,970. Matches CP-1 arithmetic; the denominator caveat is CP5-001.

- Discrete interest paid used in CP5-001: Q2 2026 = 4,958 - 2,689 = 2,269 (10-Q Q2 page 4 and 10-Q Q1 page 3); Q3 2026 = 13,587 - 4,958 = 8,629 (10-Q Q3 page 4). The jump is consistent with, but does not prove, inclusion of the roughly USD 7 million of financing costs.
- Illustrative bound: (85,000 + 900,000) / 305,677 = 3.22x. Matches CP-1; it is Assumption-Based.
- Consideration check: 0.9 + 1.4 = 2.3 billion against approximately 2.35 billion stated.
- Quote check: all quoted passages in the four handoffs were matched as exact substrings of the pinned text, apart from labels.
